conviction_note: One substantive unaggregated positive (committed backlog has nearly doubled YoY, visible only in a 10-Q footnote and cited by none of the August upgrade notes) netted against one dated negative (the reported quarter is literally the CRO handover quarter) and against a baseline that already carries a +23% 20-day run-up and a 14.49% symmetric implied move; the net is small and deliberately far inside the implied move.

findings.finding: MongoDB's contracted remaining performance obligation stood at $1,458.6m at 30 Apr 2026 against $774.3m a year earlier (+88%) while revenue grew 25%, with the duration lengthening (53% due in the next 12 months vs 58% a year ago; 46% in 13-36 months vs 38%) and non-current deferred revenue up from $24.3m to $91.2m — so committed next-12-month revenue rose roughly 72% YoY, a visibility base far larger than the market's pure 'Atlas consumption' framing assumes and the main reason a bigger-than-usual FY27 raise is mechanically available.
findings.source_date: 2026-04-30 (period end; reported in the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001441816/000162828026039150/mdb-20260430.htm, prior-year figure at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1441816/000144181625000118/mdb-20250430.htm)
findings.why_not_priced: The number appears only in a footnote MongoDB itself discourages using ('the amount and timing of revenue recognition are generally dependent upon customers' future consumption, which is inherently variable'); it is absent from every earnings press release. Two things would look different if it were priced: (a) the stock would not have fallen 22.24% on the 2 Mar 2026 print, the very quarter in which RPO stepped up $478m sequentially from $994.3m to $1,472.7m, with the coverage of that day framed entirely as an Atlas-growth-guide disappointment; and (b) the August 2026 wave of price-target raises — Stifel to $475 on 'hyperscaler results and consumption trends', Citizens to $519 on '15 data points... improved sales attainment', RBC to $515 'on Atlas growth', Guggenheim to $560 on modelled Atlas +29% — would cite backlog or committed contract value. Not one of them does; every published rationale is a consumption or channel-check argument, i.e. the market re-rated the variable half of the revenue base and ignored the contracted half.
findings.independence: Management's own Q4 FY26 call attributes the FY26 cash-flow and collections outperformance to 'higher-than-expected multiyear EA deals' — an independent confirmation from a different document that large multi-year commitments were signed in the window RPO jumped: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/03/02/mongodb-mdb-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ . A third, much lower-circulation source (a 13 Jun 2026 readout of the BofA and William Blair conferences) has management flagging 'upside from unpredictable on-premise contract wins' after the May guide was set: https://www.stockmarketnerd.com/mongodb-june-2026-investor-conference-review/ . CAVEAT I am stating rather than hiding: because much of this backlog is multi-year Enterprise Advanced, and management has said on-prem should fall from 25% to 10% of the business, the read-through is to total revenue and to guidance headroom, not to the Atlas growth rate the market is actually trading — which is why I have capped this at +2.5 rather than sizing it against the 14.49% implied move.

findings.finding: The quarter being reported (fiscal Q2, May-July 2026) is precisely MongoDB's go-to-market handover quarter: incoming CRO Ryan Mac Ban started 27 Apr 2026 and the 24 Mar 2026 release states 'Outgoing CRO Paul Capombassis will support a seamless transition to Mac Ban through Q2', while the President of Field Operations, Cedric Pech, resigned effective 15 Apr 2026 and product leadership was split into two new Chief Product Officers on 22 Apr 2026 — i.e. a full field-and-product leadership rebuild landing inside the reported quarter, with a new CEO only ten months in.
findings.why_not_priced: The individual appointments were wired in March/April and the exec departures were part of why the stock fell 22% on 2 Mar 2026 — but the price then was $252.73 and the stock is now $440.92 after a +23% 20-day run and a set of upgrades whose stated basis is consumption data, not sales-organisation continuity. If this risk were still in the price the 25-delta skew would not be flat at -0.17 vol points on a name whose two worst prints in the sample (-26.94% and -22.24%) were both go-to-market/guidance events; someone would be paying for the tail. The specific, checkable detail that the departing CRO's overlap ran 'through Q2' — meaning two CROs and no field-ops president across the whole selling quarter — is in a single press release and appears in none of the previews.
findings.independence: CUTS AGAINST IT, and I am reporting that: Citizens' 19 Aug 2026 note says its diligence produced 15 data points, 14 positive, including 'evidence of improved sales attainment in the second fiscal quarter' — https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/citizens-raises-mongodb-stock-price-target-on-improved-sales-data-93CH-4866696 . That is why this is sized at -1.0 rather than larger. Corroborating the facts themselves (not the impact): the 8-K of 2026-03-02 documents Pech's resignation effective 15 Apr 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1441816/000162828026013199/mdb-20260302.htm ; the two-CPO split is dated 22 Apr 2026 at https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/mongodb-names-two-chief-product-officers-in-leadership-reshuffle-93CH-4629374 .

searched_and_found_nothing: Atlas incident/status history for May-July 2026 (the fiscal quarter): only short minor incidents (Azure West Europe stream-processing errors and a free/flex config delay, both 29 Jul 2026, resolved in hours; a Voyage AI elevated-error incident 27 Jul 2026) — nothing consumption-material. https://status.mongodb.com/history

Atlas changelog and pricing pages for a price increase, tier repricing or deprecation inside the quarter: only additive/free features (Vector Search source-field storage, automated embedding preview, extended AWS Gen2 standard IOPS, new payment methods). No pricing action found. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/release-notes/changelog/

Hiring-trend read: MongoDB's Greenhouse board shows ~82 open roles today across Atlas Core Data Services, Atlas Search, AI Builder Experience, sales development and technical services — but the Wayback Machine has no archived snapshot of the careers page for 2026-06-01, so there is no comparable prior count and no trend can be established. Dropped rather than guessed. https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/mongodb/jobs and http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=mongodb.com/company/careers/jobs&timestamp=20260601

Customer-side distress: no dated 2026 forum/Reddit thread found describing Atlas billing shocks or migrations off Atlas in the quarter; the only structural billing change found (serverless retirement, 22 Jan 2026) predates the quarter.

Activist / ownership: no 13D. The only activist-adjacent datapoint is a $145m ValueAct 13F position dated Q2 2025 — stale and non-controlling. https://www.boardroomalpha.com/activist-investors-shake-up-portfolios-q2-2025-13f-highlights/

Insider Form 4 clusters: routine RSU tax-withholding dispositions only, e.g. CEO CJ Desai 3,913 shares at $335.90 on 2026-07-01. No open-market selling cluster into the run-up. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001441816/000162828026047295/wk-form4_1783369943.xml

Quiet 8-K / pre-announcement / capital raise: MongoDB's last 8-K is 2026-07-06 and contains only annual-meeting results and the supermajority-removal charter amendment effective 2026-07-01. Nothing operational. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001441816/000162828026047228/mdb-20260630.htm

Sales-organisation health via RepVue: AE quota attainment ~49%, in line with the 40-55% 2026 B2B SaaS benchmark, so no deterioration signal; the company page rate-limited (HTTP 429) on repeated attempts. https://www.repvue.com/companies/MongoDB

Competitive displacement evidence: Snowflake Postgres went GA 24 Feb 2026 and Snowflake has hardened it through 2026, but I found no dated 2026 evidence of MongoDB workload loss to it. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2026/other/2026-02-24-snowflake-postgres-ga
Buyback as a support mechanism: pace is only ~$100m/quarter ($100.0m in Q1 FY27, $499.7m authorisation remaining at 30 Apr 2026) against a ~$36bn market cap — immaterial to a reaction-day move.
baseline_tension: My one real finding is a positive on a name already up 23.17% in 20 days and 6.6% off its high, which agrees with the market's refusal to pay for downside (skew -0.17 vol points) but cuts against reading the run-up as leaving no fundamental room; the sharper tension is that the 14.49% event-implied move sits well below the 19.58% median of MDB's own last eight reactions, so the market is under-paying for tails on a name whose published bar is now explicit (Stifel, 18 Aug 2026, at a lower spot: H2 guidance likely needs to go to '25%-plus' to support the stock) — hence a small positive point estimate with a wide honest band rather than any attempt to beat the straddle.
